meaning: poplar tree; also the surname Yang
conceptZh: 橡膠恐龍的小短手按不到澆水壺的小按鈕，調皮小老鼠自信地退到畫面最左邊全力衝刺，結果衝過頭彈到恐龍圓肚子上又飛回來、腳底冒煙撞倒花盆，小楊樹苗、方形太陽燈、木板和噴出的三道水花全被撞飛，剛好排成楊字，最後小老鼠輕輕一點按鈕，筆畫就啪一聲鎖成鮮綠色的楊。
object: a tiny poplar sapling in a pot, a boxy hanging sun-lamp, a wooden shelf plank and a watering can with one tiny button
morph: the mouse's overshoot crash springs the sapling upright into the wood radical 木 on the left; the sun-lamp drops into the square 日 top-right, the shelf plank falls flat as the horizontal stroke beneath it, and the tipped watering can sprays one hooked arc and three slanting streaks that freeze as 勿 below, completing 楊
creativeAngle: 全新的「太用力」物理笑點，取代前一版安靜的忍者熊貓跳樹。笑點直接長在字義上：楊樹要曬太陽、要澆水，右邊的昜就由方形太陽燈（日）、木板（一）和水花（勿）撞出來，左邊的木就是楊樹苗本身。小老鼠「一步領先」的個性變成衝太快、衝過頭的笑料；恐龍的小短手提供動機，且只有兩個角色加一組道具，畫面乾淨。三次語音各對應一個畫面動作。
promptEn:
8-second 2D cartoon clip, bright soft-shaded toy-world look, pale cream-yellow background, nothing busy behind. Only two characters and one cluster of props.

Cast: a tiny cheeky cartoon mouse (original design) with huge round ears, a lightning-fast grin and a long whippy tail; a chubby rubber dinosaur (original design) with enormous feet and comically tiny arms. Props, center frame: a small potted poplar sapling on the left, and on the right a boxy hanging sun-lamp above a short wooden shelf plank, with a red watering can on the plank that has ONE tiny green button on its handle.

0.0-1.5s WANT IT: the dinosaur strains toward the tiny button with its stubby arms, grunting, fingertips a whole hand short. The mouse zips in from the left in a speed blur, stops on a dime, points at the button, cracks its tiny knuckles and winks: this is a one-finger job.

1.5-3.5s TOO MUCH POWER: the mouse backs up all the way to the far left edge, scrapes one foot like a bull, ears pinned back. Off-screen voice: "楊" (ㄧㄤˊ) exactly as it launches. It rockets right in a blur, flies straight past the button, and BOINGs off the dinosaur's round rubber belly with a cartoon squash-and-stretch, ricocheting back across the frame.

3.5-5.0s THE BIG CRASH: the mouse skids backwards on smoking feet, leaves two little skid marks, and BONKs into the pot. Everything hops in the air. The sapling springs bolt upright into the wood radical 木 on the left (trunk, crossbar, two spreading roots). The sun-lamp drops and squares into the sun shape 日 top-right, the shelf plank lands flat as a single horizontal stroke beneath it, and the tipped watering can sprays one hooked arc and three slanting water streaks that hang frozen as 勿 below. Dizzy mouse, spiral eyes, happy wobble.

5.0-5.4s PAYOFF: the mouse reaches up and gently taps the button with one fingertip. Off-screen voice: "楊" (ㄧㄤˊ) as every piece snaps into saturated deep forest-green solid strokes, forming the exact standard Traditional Chinese character 楊: wood radical 木 on the left, 昜 on the right (日 on top, one horizontal stroke, 勿 at the bottom). The glyph is centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with clean margins, and holds perfectly still from 5.0s to 8.0s.

5.4-8.0s HOLD: the glyph does not move. At the bottom-right, well clear of the strokes, the mouse hoists a tiny potted poplar sapling overhead like a trophy. Off-screen voice at 6.5s: "楊樹" (ㄧㄤˊ ㄕㄨˋ) exactly as the sapling pops out a few fluttering silver-green leaves. Bottom-left, the dinosaur gives a stubby-armed thumbs-up and does a happy foot stomp. One wink from the mouse at 7.8s.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly this line and nothing else, slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between utterances: 楊、楊、楊樹 (ㄧㄤˊ、ㄧㄤˊ、ㄧㄤˊ ㄕㄨˋ). Soft cartoon boing, skid and bonk sounds under the voice, quieter than it. No other dialogue, no music louder than the voice.

The only on-screen text is the single glyph 楊. No subtitles, no other letters or words, no watermark, no flashing. Bright but not neon, no pure white blowout, no dark grading. No real people or realistic human figures; characters are a cartoon mouse and a rubber toy dinosaur only.
